response.note_text:
Subjective: 53F c/o chest pain x3 months. Dull, pressure-like CP brought on by walking; limiting her walking. No radiation. Currently pain-free; no SOB, sweats or clamminess now. PMH: DM on metformin, no N/V/D or med side effects; BG slightly higher d/t reduced activity; trying with diet, likes sodas. Last HbA1c 7.0. Ophthalmology appt in 2 wks. Elevated BP documented by other clinicians with upward trend, not formally diagnosed, no BP meds; pt unaware. FHx heart disease.
Objective: EKG in office: normal, no signs of MI. Exam: no JVD, no neck swelling, no carotid bruits. Lungs clear, no crackles or rhonchi. Heart RRR, 2/6 systolic ejection murmur (known). Pulses equal. Abd soft, NT, no guarding, no masses. Back normal. Ext: 1+ nonpitting edema ankles, no calf tenderness.
Assessment: 1. Chest pain, suspected unstable angina (DM, suspected HTN, FHx heart disease); concern for blockage. 2. DM, doing fairly well. 3. Elevated BP trend, likely HTN; LE edema.
Plan: 1. Refer cardiology, aim next wk; stress test. Start ASA 81 mg daily. Rx SL NTG prn CP: if CP stops with rest, no NTG needed; if CP persists, take 1 tab, may repeat q5min up to 3 tabs; if not relieved, call 911 / go to hospital. 2. Continue metformin 500 mg BID. Keep ophthalmology appt for diabetic retinopathy exam. HbA1c today. Avoid soda and sweets; resume exercise once cardiac w/u done. 3. Start low-dose HCTZ (also for LE swelling). Home BP cuff, daily AM log, enter in MyChart. Counselled on SE: increased evening urination, possible cross-reaction with sulfa meds; handout given. F/u 2 wks.
